name: Abha City Centre
tagline: The core around the old market and the main streets
description: The commercial heart of the city, with the Tuesday market, the shopping streets and most of the mid-range hotels. It is where the practical business of Abha happens and where a stay without a car is most workable, though the hills make walking hard work.
bestFor: Shorter stays and anyone without a vehicle
pros: Markets, shops and services all close
The widest hotel choice in the city
cons: Traffic congestion in the summer season
Little green space in the centre itself

name: Al Sudah
tagline: The high escarpment above the city
description: The mountain area northwest of Abha, rising past three thousand metres to the highest point in Saudi Arabia, with the cable car dropping down the escarpment and juniper forest along the ridge. Summer visitors fill the parks and viewpoints here to escape the lowland heat.
bestFor: Anyone here for the landscape rather than the city
pros: The best views and coolest air in Saudi Arabia
cons: Thirty minutes from the city by road
Extremely busy in the summer season
Cold and often in cloud outside summer

name: Abha Dam and Al Sahab
tagline: The lake and the ridge above it
description: The area around the Abha Dam reservoir southwest of the centre, with lakeside parks, cafes on the ridge and some of the better residential streets. The cloud that gives Al Sahab its name rolls through here on summer afternoons, which is the local spectacle.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a view and space away from the centre
pros: Lake, parks and viewpoints on the doorstep
cons: Needs a car for anything practical
Fills with domestic visitors in summer

name: Khamis Mushait
tagline: The larger twin city with the airport
description: A city of its own about twenty-five kilometres east, larger than Abha and considerably cheaper, with more shopping, the regional airport nearby and a flatter, hotter setting off the escarpment. Many people who work in Abha live here for the price difference.
bestFor: Budget-conscious longer stays with a car
pros: Cheaper rents and food than Abha
cons: Hotter and less scenic than Abha
Thirty minutes to Abha by road

name: Rijal Almaa
tagline: The stone tower village down the escarpment
description: A heritage village about an hour away on the Tihamah side of the mountains, built of stone and quartz tower houses stacked on the slope, and one of the most photographed places in Saudi Arabia. A few guesthouses have opened, and the road down is spectacular.
bestFor: A few nights among the towers rather than a working base
pros: The escarpment road is a genuine experience
Far quieter than Abha in summer
cons: An hour of mountain driving from the city
Almost no services beyond the village
Hotter than Abha at the lower elevation
